authority.rule: When documentation conflicts with current source/runtime behavior, current source wins.

capabilityContract.rule: Shared field names keep shared semantics even when individual getCapabilities objects expose different subsets and API-specific fields.

fields.enabled: Current Execution policy or authorization permits use of the capability.
fields.supported: The selected Runtime, platform, or backend has an implementation.
fields.configured: Required static selection, profile, or configuration is complete enough to attempt a call.
fields.available: Known current executability. null means intentionally not established by this side-effect-free probe, not false.
fields.reason: Machine-readable explanation when the owning API exposes a disabled, unsupported, or unavailable reason.
fields.checked: Whether the owning API performed the deeper probe it defines; static configuration alone must not imply true.
fields.authenticated: Authentication state only when reliably known; unknown means it was not probed.

cli.runtimeMode: Use the default JavaScript Runtime. Do not add the compatibility-only -stack flag to new commands.

appMode.runtimeMode: One execution-owned App Shell and one existing Goja Runtime. validate, doctor, and build use authoritative package validation and never execute entry JavaScript; build copies a same-platform installed Runtime template and does not cross-build.

aiCli.purpose: Low-token desktop tool surface for coding agents; reuses Stable Runtime services and Execution evidence.

protectedPackages.purpose: Publish, license, activate, and execute OpenDesk protected packages; authoring workflows continue to produce ordinary JavaScript.

runtimeRules: For coding-agent desktop interaction, inspect `opendesk ai schema` and `opendesk ai capabilities`; prefer its window metadata, targeted screenshots, deterministic primitives, and reusable recipes before full-screen visual reasoning.
Prefer stable documented APIs for new scripts.

Treat JavaScript compatibility as a tested feature baseline, not an edition-wide claim. The language gate covers selected ES2015-ES2023 authoring syntax and built-ins; script-level await in ordinary .js files is provided by the OpenDesk execution wrapper and is not ESM. .mjs entrypoints support static relative import/export, nested static module graphs, and supported package resolution within the same Execution. Runtime import(), ESM module-level top-level await, Node built-in modules, native .node addons, remote URL modules, and automatic npm install remain unsupported. require/module/exports are reserved implementation compatibility globals rather than public APIs.

getCapabilities methods are diagnostic and context-discovery APIs by default, not mandatory handshakes before every business call. Prefer the normal business method first unless the specific API contract requires capability-based branching.
Prefer page.ensurePermissions for permission-gated desktop workflows.
For external desktop UI, prefer UI.findText/UI.tapText and Geometry over direct OCR bbox clicking. Use Vision.runOCR for raw OCR; Vision.detectUI is a deprecated image-local compatibility helper.
Use ImageColor as a secondary pixel/template/color primitive, not as a replacement for semantic verification.

Prefer axios for normal script HTTP requests; axios is a polyfill backed by http.request. Use http.download only for host-authorized native streaming GET downloads; local CLI and ai run enable it, while HTTP, MCP, Scheduler, generic Runtime, JavaScript options, and environment variables cannot grant it.

NativeExtensions is an Experimental manifest-discovered immutable binding. Normal local CLI calls use NativeExtensions.<namespace>.<method>(businessParams) with routes fixed by the Host; it discovers only the program-relative bundle directory by default. HTTP and MCP cannot enable or call it. The low-level NativeExtension.call compatibility surface requires the separate -experimental-unsafe-native-extension-call local diagnostic gate.

Accessibility is an execution-owned Experimental local Runtime API. Trusted local script and AI CLI entrypoints explicitly enable it; HTTP, MCP, Scheduler, and generic Runtime initialization leave it disabled. Every traversal requires an explicit window, execution-owned element ref, or App target scope. It never silently falls back to OCR or mouse input.

Uppercase UI operates visible targets in external desktop apps. Lowercase ui owns OpenDesk-created surfaces and is dormant by default; enable it with -ui or strict clawdesk.runtime.json. Prefer ui.toast for transient feedback and ui.createWindow for custom windows. ui.notify is a compatibility alias for ui.toast, while the global notify() function sends operating-system notifications.

Uppercase App controls external desktop applications. automation.app controls only the current explicit -app execution, remains fail-closed in ordinary Script/HTTP/MCP/Scheduler modes, and never starts a second Runtime for tray actions or activation.

Dialog is always present but fail-closed without the ui capability. Its alert, confirm, and prompt methods are asynchronous native modal dialogs; global alert/confirm/prompt are thin polyfill aliases, never browser-style blocking calls.
Omit -stack for new scripts. The old upgraded/playwright values and browser/context-shaped globals are implementation compatibility residue, not maintained user APIs or a browser engine.

Use the frozen Execution.env snapshot for local project and inherited OS environment values. Local executions merge .env, .opendesk.env, then the environment supplied when the OpenDesk process started; they do not parse shell startup files. Windows names are uppercase. Remote and scheduled executions do not inherit host environment secrets.

Command is an execution-owned native command runner, not Node.js child_process. Local -script and ai run executions enable it by default; HTTP, MCP, and Scheduler executions disable it. Use Command.run(executable,args,options) without shell command interpolation.

LLM.generate is an execution-scoped HTTP model facade with no Agent tools or file authority. Exactly one of prompt/messages is required. Both OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions adapters reject refusal, truncation, empty/malformed terminal output, and strictly validate structured result.data without coercion.

Agent.run is a thin Codex or Claude Code CLI adapter over the existing Command owner. Builtin profiles resolve only fixed codex/claude names from the current Execution PATH when no absolute executable override exists; the native Command owner enforces PATH/PATHEXT, platform executability, and absolute output without a shell. Codex is never auto-installed, auto-logged-in, or used as fallback after another backend fails. Agent accepts no raw CLI arguments. Codex uses fixed feature-disable arguments for shell, unified exec, computer use, browser/in-app automation, apps, and multi-agent; Claude uses an empty tool allowlist and strict empty MCP configuration.

LLM and Agent return {data,meta} through one schema-validation and ModelCallError contract. requestedModel is configuration; meta.model and usage are backend facts and remain null when unreported. Timeout covers preparation through validation and aborts the native HTTP request or Command process group.

SQLite is a first-party, Promise-only local Runtime API, not a Native Extension. Use SQLite.open({path, mode}) and the returned handle's query/exec/batch/close methods with bound parameters; it is enabled only for trusted local script/AI executions and is absent from HTTP, MCP, and Scheduler to avoid granting remote filesystem database access.

Recorder is one execution-owned local Runtime object. Global input capture requires the explicit trusted local -allow-recorder-capture flag; within is initial provenance rather than a persistent input filter, and action-level application/window context supports intentional app and window switches. Ordinary hover motion is filtered, while button-held motion is retained. target-semantics records label-only point-hit Accessibility evidence and bubbles through at most six parents to the nearest actionable control, without pointer AX values, screenshots, OCR, or trees. Final editable-value sampling additionally requires captureKeyboard:true plus keyboardContent:non-sensitive-test, rejects secure fields, and overrides related low-level key evidence. When a target does not expose a final editable value, complete Basic Latin KEY_TYPED facts may become an explicitly editable keyboard.type variable even for input-method, unknown, or legacy non-commit evidence; that fallback is low-level input, not verified committed text, and requires human-to-recipe review or parameterization plus an independent production oracle. A raw-prefix pointer tail that began before listener readiness is explicitly excluded only when it belongs to one held button and a matching release proves return to a neutral pointer state. Unrepresentable composition/dead keys, in-session incomplete pairing, unclosed or ambiguous start tails, and missing action context become explicit action-local omissions: actions readiness is needs-review; explicit basic generation may emit a warned partial candidate while default semantic generation blocks. Event loss, untrusted raw/manifest state, and unverifiable Custom UI control boundaries remain package-level blocked failures. Repeated same-key presses followed by one release become a bounded repeatCount. HTTP, MCP, Scheduler, JavaScript options, and environment variables cannot grant capture. Recorder.buildActions and Recorder.generateScript remain available without capture permission, reread fixed files, never call a model, never overwrite an existing candidate, and never auto-replay.

Use the native lowercase path global for platform path-string operations. path.resolve and path.relative use the immutable Execution.workdir, not the host process cwd; path never performs filesystem I/O or symlink resolution.
Do not use retired TestMonkey documentation as a current API authority.

UI.tapTexts defaults to intervalMs=300, waitForEach=true, timeout=10000 per step and polling=200. Exact unpositioned ordinary activation uses Runtime-owned auto resolution: OCR first, then complete authorized native evidence only when OCR is missing or ambiguous before input. Callers do not configure resolver strategy or fallback order. Constraints, state errors and submitted inputs never trigger unsafe retries. Bound one current window; preserve completed input and actionState. Business results require independent reads.

UI.getValue and UI.setValue are Experimental local native text-value helpers. They require explicit Accessibility scope, preserve string values exactly, use one managed ref per call, and never fall back to OCR, keyboard, focus, scrolling, or retries.

UI.tapTargets is an Experimental semantic activation API: use {text}, {role,name}, or {identifier} exact P0 targets without strategy/fallback/provider/coordinate policy. Runtime resolves text-only targets through OCR first and may use exact Accessibility name lookup only after a deterministic pre-input OCR discovery failure; role/name/identifier constraints go directly to Accessibility and are never discarded. Submitted mouse/native input and native actionState=unknown stop immediately with no retry. The legacy all-{locator} overload remains Accessibility-first with required resolved WindowInfo, complete preflight/fixed refs, optional refocus='if-needed', and no OCR/mouse fallback.

globals.name: page
globals.summary: Desktop page entry: screenshot, open URL/App, waits and permissions.
globals.waitSemantics: waitFor dispatches number waits to waitForTimeout and predicates to waitForFunction, forwarding their options. waitForTimeout supports AbortSignal and resolves asynchronously even for 0ms. waitForFunction has an independent deadline and one predicate call in flight; predicate throws/rejections remain transient. waitForAll preserves order, values, identity, and raw rejection reasons, treats functions as values, and never cancels caller-owned work. Duration, timeout, and polling are finite numbers in inclusive 0..86400000; fractional values are accepted and Timer converts them to integer milliseconds. Function/all timeout 0 rejects with TimeoutError/TIMEOUT; signal cancellation rejects with AbortError/CANCELED; invalid arguments use INVALID_ARGUMENT. Every terminal path removes wait-owned timers and listeners.

globals.name: Geometry
globals.coordinateSpace: Consumes WindowInfo, DisplayInfo, or tagged screen regions and emits only tagged virtual-desktop logical screen points/regions. It never accepts a bare bbox as screen coordinates.

globals.name: Accessibility
globals.source: execution-owned native Runtime + macOS AX / Windows UIA backend
globals.authorization: Enabled only by trusted local script and AI CLI execution.Request values. Disabled operations reject without native target reads; getCapabilities remains available and never prompts or crawls the desktop.
globals.capabilities: getCapabilities returns schemaVersion, platform/backend, hostAuthorization.enabled, implementation {available,status,menus,actions,coordinateMapping,notes}, permission {required,state,granted,cached}, top-level available, fixed limits, and cancellation.hardCancel=false. implementation.actions is a per-action boolean map and does not promise element-level support.
globals.scope: Every snapshot/find call requires an existing OpenDeskWindowInfo, an element ref owned by the current execution, or {app: OpenDeskAppTarget, root: application|menuBar}. No implicit whole-desktop traversal.
globals.limits: One total 3000ms default/30000ms maximum deadline including queue time; maxDepth 8/32, maxNodes 1000/5000, 256 active refs, and 32 queued requests per execution.
globals.identity: Element refs are opaque execution-owned objects bound to the process/container/native element. Their public fields cannot be serialized and reconstructed as authority.
globals.actions: invoke, setValue, expand, collapse, select, and setChecked use native capability/state checks and never auto-retry or fall back to pointer input after an attempted action.
globals.lifecycle: Workers, pending/queued requests, refs, and native resources are canceled, joined, counted, and released by the owning execution; hardCancel is false.
globals.coordinates: nativeBounds stays tagged in the backend coordinate space. bounds is null unless a reliable conversion to OpenDesk logical screen coordinates was performed.

globals.name: UI
globals.source: visual polyfills 006-ui/011-ui-targets/012-ui-scope-locator/013-ui-perception plus execution-owned native Accessibility value, target-sequence, menu composition, and privacy-gated DesktopVision observation

scopeLocator.identity: UI.within synchronously snapshots one resolved WindowInfo identity. Each later Scope or Locator operation refreshes the same id, PID and native handle, so move/resize refreshes geometry while closure/recreation or a same-title replacement fails STALE_TARGET without rebinding.
scopeLocator.locator: A Locator copies only Scope identity and target description. It retains no OCR point, screenshot, ElementRef or ElementHandle; find returns a one-time observation snapshot rather than an executable object.
scopeLocator.targets: {text} uses existing OCR/visual discovery, {image} uses existing high-confidence (0.95) image discovery, and role/name/identifier uses exact native Accessibility. Loss of the native UI tree does not disable text/image observation or action.
scopeLocator.find: A complete reliable zero result is null; a unique result is TargetMatch; ambiguity and incomplete search remain AMBIGUOUS_TARGET and SEARCH_INCOMPLETE. Permission/backend failures are never converted to null.
scopeLocator.waitFor: exists and visible use repeated readonly observations under one total deadline. Cancellation, stale identity, ambiguity, incomplete search and terminal observation failures stop immediately. Semantic visible is NOT_SUPPORTED unless native evidence can prove it.
scopeLocator.tap: Semantic, text and image actions delegate once to UI.tapTargets, UI.tapText and UI.tapImage respectively. No secondary click engine, submitted-action fallback or replay is introduced; actionState, completed prefix, cancellation and cleanup remain owner-defined.
scopeLocator.value: getValue/setValue delegate only to the existing strict native textField owner. Visual/OCR results never become a native value; there is no keyboard fallback.

globals.coordinateMapping: Every discovery uses a fresh explicit screen clip. imageWidth/logicalScope.width and imageHeight/logicalScope.height are separately calculated actual capture scales; a scope across effective different-DPI displays fails closed.

value.scope: Both methods require an explicit native Accessibility scope and a selector resolving to exactly one textField. They do not launch, focus, scroll, expand, type, press Enter, or wait for a future control.
value.read: getValue returns only the native string value, preserving empty strings, leading zeroes, Unicode, whitespace, and newlines. It does not substitute name, visible text, OCR, or numeric coercion, and readable fields need not be writable.
value.write: setValue accepts only a complete string, performs native setValue at most once through the same execution-owned ref, then strictly reads that ref back. An explicit enabled=false rejects; when enabled is unavailable, only the same Accessibility owner's exposed setValue action proves writability, and perform revalidates native state before submission. Native actionState is preserved separately from verified; matching readback never upgrades unknown to acknowledged and no verification failure triggers a replay.
value.deadline: One total timeout defaults to 3000ms and is capped at 30000ms. Remaining budgets decrease across locate, precondition/action, and verification; expiry before perform is called is not_started. Cleanup is separately bounded by the execution-owned Accessibility.release path and does not pretend to be cancellation of the earlier native action. This is a bound on the current operation, not an auto-wait contract.
value.authorization: Available only through the local execution-owned native Accessibility capability and host permission. signal and unknown options are rejected before native input; there is no Promise.race-only cancellation or visual/keyboard fallback.

tapTexts.interval: Extra milliseconds after the previous input returns and before the next observation; none before the first or after the last step. Explicit 0 disables this extra wait.
tapTexts.waiting: Experimental per-step target wait, enabled by default. Each step budget starts after intervalMs and is checked before/after observation and before input. Poll only successful zero-match observations. Ambiguity, invalid explicit index, target loss, screenshot/OCR failure and input errors are terminal.
tapTexts.scope: With waiting enabled, use a resolved WindowInfo or omit within to bind the first active window. Preserve id, PID, title and available handle throughout this sequence, refresh same-window bounds, and retain foreground checks. No implicit launch/focus or selection of a replacement window. Static regions remain snapshots.
tapTexts.cancellation: signal accepts AbortSignal or null. Cancel delays and prevent later stages/input; synchronous native work cannot be forcibly interrupted. Never retry submitted input. If a successful input returns after cancellation, retain it in completed before rejecting.
tapTexts.result: Promise<{ok:true, action:'tapTexts', completed:OpenDeskUITapResult[]}>; not an array. Step failures carry failedIndex, failedText, failedPhase interval|locate|input, completed and cause.
tapTexts.compatibility: Default interval changed from 0 to 300 and target waiting is now enabled. Explicit waitForEach:false plus intervalMs:0 restores fail-fast timing and permits legacy Display/ScreenRegion scope. Unknown options, symbol fields, sparse strings and invalid timing are rejected before input.
tapTexts.verification: Text visibility is not proof of enabled state or business completion. Verify postconditions independently; do not use an unknown input outcome as permission to replay. Runtime/native verification remains separate from source-level isolated tests.

tapTargets.preferredInput: A non-empty sequence of exact P0 semantic {text?,role?,name?,identifier?} targets. text-only targets keep ordinary business code small; native fields are exact AND constraints. Caller options are only within?: resolved WindowInfo, timeout?: 1..30000, and signal?: AbortSignal|null. strategy, fallback, provider, confidence, bounds and coordinates are rejected before observation/input.
tapTargets.resolverPolicy: Runtime resolves the active window once when within is omitted. A text-only step first uses UI.tapText exact OCR. Only deterministic pre-input OCR discovery failures (TARGET_NOT_FOUND, AMBIGUOUS_TARGET, OCR_FAILED, SCREENSHOT_FAILED and safe scope/coordinate failures) may fall through to exact Accessibility name=text. Any role/name/identifier makes Accessibility authoritative immediately; supplied native evidence is never discarded for OCR.
tapTargets.actionSafety: A successful OCR click is recorded before cancellation is honored. Submitted mouse input, submitted native invoke, actionState=unknown, or any uncertain action state stops that target and all later targets; no resolver retry, mouse/coordinate fallback, or replay is allowed. Accessibility requires a unique enabled invokable element and treats acknowledged/not_needed as success; an acknowledged receipt remains completed if later release cleanup fails.
tapTargets.result: Promise<{ok:true,action:'tapTargets',completed:[{index,resolver:'ocr',action:'click',backend,...}|{index,resolver:'accessibility',action:'invoke',backend,requestId,actionState}]}>. Failures retain failedIndex, failedTarget, failedPhase, completed, attempts[{resolver,phase,code,...}], cause and possible cleanupError; cleanup after an acknowledged action reports the receipt in completed.
tapTargets.legacyCompatibility: An all-{locator: OpenDeskAccessibilitySelector} sequence preserves the original Accessibility-first overload: explicit resolved WindowInfo, full distinct-locator preflight before input, fixed managed refs, exact window revalidation, maxDepth/maxNodes, optional refocus, structured legacy errors and at-most-once invoke. Semantic and legacy steps cannot mix; legacy never falls back to OCR/mouse.

relativeTextTargeting.requiresWithin: Using region or relativeTo requires an explicit within: OpenDeskWindowInfo so the Runtime can preserve and revalidate window identity.
relativeTextTargeting.region: A tagged OpenDeskScreenRegion snapshot or a synchronous (currentWin: OpenDeskWindowInfo) => OpenDeskScreenRegion rule. Dynamic rules are recomputed once per fresh observation; static regions never track moved windows.
relativeTextTargeting.relativeTo: Uses one exact text anchor from the same capture and Vision.runOCR result. Choose either direction with inclusive maxGap/minOverlap filtering, or a synchronous anchor => tagged screen region whose final intersection must fully contain each target bbox. It never auto-selects the nearest or first candidate.
relativeTextTargeting.spatialUnits: All gaps, overlap calculations, and regions use Geometry desktop logical screen coordinates; never multiply or divide them by Display.scale. Spatial predicates use the continuous logical projection of OCR bboxes before public bounds are outward-rounded; callbacks still receive the public target shape.
relativeTextTargeting.disambiguation: The anchor must be unique and top-level index applies only after target relationship filtering. Missing anchors follow each read method's no-result contract, while single clicks fail TARGET_NOT_FOUND with stage=anchor; tapTexts waiting may poll a missing anchor. Multiple anchors fail AMBIGUOUS_TARGET with stage=anchor.
relativeTextTargeting.freshness: Revalidate the specified window before capture and after recognition. Dynamic or absent outer regions permit at most one complete pre-input re-observation after same-window bounds changes; static regions fail stale. Never retry after mouse input has been invoked.
relativeTextTargeting.unsupportedBehavior: Passing region or relativeTo to an unsupported method fails with INVALID_ARGUMENT before observation or input. Image and Accessibility anchors are not supported.

menu.scope: Requires a resolved OpenDeskWindowInfo or {app: OpenDeskAppTarget, root: menuBar}; read methods never expand or focus menus.
menu.path: A non-empty complete hierarchy path whose segments are non-empty strings or exact {name?,identifier?} AND selectors.
menu.action: tapMenuItem serially expands freshly observed unique levels under one total deadline, then submits invoke/select/setChecked at most once through the same AccessibilityRuntime.
menu.compatibility: Existing UI text/image methods retain their screenshot, OCR, image and mouse contracts; they are not silently replaced with native Accessibility actions.

globals.name: Recorder
globals.source: native execution owner + static libuiohook adapter + JavaScript facade
globals.captureAuthorization: Only a trusted local -script invocation with -allow-recorder-capture may start the process-wide listener. The option object and Execution.env cannot grant capture.
globals.captureScope: within requires an exact initial foreground PID and title as provenance. The listener is desktop-global after start: application/window switches are retained as action-level contexts rather than filtered, and pause/resume does not rebind or enforce the initial window. This is not an OS-level hook filter.
globals.platformBehavior: macOS and Windows use the same pinned libuiohook 1.2.2 adapter and data contract. Linux is X11-only. Wayland full-desktop capture is explicitly unsupported.
globals.textInput: Final text results take precedence over causal key events. Focused, writable, non-secure editable values are sampled only with both explicit keyboard options; manifests retain UTF-16LE hashes/lengths plus the necessary insertion patch rather than unchanged full context. Bounds-free editables require a name or identifier. Generated text-edit code uniquely resolves inside the current active window and verifies focus plus value hashes before and after one setValue. macOS KEY_TYPED records only a coarse keyboard-layout/input-method/unknown source category. If no final value is available, complete Basic Latin input may still become a named editable keyboard.type variable regardless of that coarse source or the non-commit gap; it remains unverified low-level input and must be reviewed or parameterized in human-to-recipe and checked by an independent oracle before production qualification. Unrepresentable composition/dead keys and structurally incomplete local evidence are omitted, leaving a generatable needs-review candidate rather than blocking unrelated actions.
globals.production: Session control uses explicit idempotent pause and resume methods; toggle is only a serialized UI adaptation. Pause retains the native hook lease, drops input content before normalization, records pause/resume boundaries, and counts against maxDurationMs. excludeControlClick consumes an unmodified live Custom UI click event and records an auditable boundary with explicit native event IDs so its pointer envelope cannot become a generated target action. buildActions rereads the actual manifest plus raw NDJSON and writes versioned actions; a missing terminal manifest or damaged final partial line yields only a validated-prefix, blocked revision. A raw-prefix partial pointer envelope that began before listener readiness is retained but excluded only after one held button and its matching neutral release are proven; the same incomplete shape later in the session is omitted with a needs-review issue. A reliably saved terminal package stopped by maximum-duration may also become needs-review; any accompanying backend, storage, event-loss, or unknown error remains blocked. A complete <=4-point libuiohook press/drag/release jitter envelope becomes an auditable click, while supported bounded straight drags remain explicit drag actions. generateScript rereads strict ready or needs-review actions, verifies their deterministic issues, omissions, and pinned raw byte reference, and emits a sleep for every non-pause inter-action gap. A needs-review revision generates a runnable partial candidate, including an explicit source warning and constraint; zero safe actions yield a warning-only no-op candidate. Package-level blocked revisions are rejected. Generation exclusively creates ordinary basic JavaScript plus a not-run candidate; it starts neither capture nor replay.

globals.name: Events
globals.source: native runtime wrapper + explicit polling backend
globals.notes: Polling is reported in capability and event payloads; no MCP/HTTP surface and no GlobalShortcut duplication. Window events are unsupported on platforms where the existing window facade is unavailable.

globals.name: App
globals.source: native Runtime wrapper + existing NSWorkspace/process/window backends
globals.identity: PID, name, bundleId, or path; stable bundle/path identity is preferred and one identity may group multiple process instances. macOS+cgo recognizes only the exact system aliases 计算器 and Calculator, each normalized to com.apple.calculator; explicit bundleId/path/PID targets and unknown names are never translated
globals.readiness: process or an existing Window-facade row owned by a matching PID; custom predicates are explicitly unsupported
globals.lifecycle: Promise workers are execution-scoped, context-cancelable, timeout-bounded, and joined during Runtime teardown
globals.compatibility: page.openApp and AI CLI app.open retain their public contract while sharing the same launch bridge; System process and Window APIs remain independent
globals.platformBehavior: macOS+cgo uses NSWorkspace/Open/NSRunningApplication and recognizes the documented Calculator aliases through the existing bundle-ID launcher; macOS without cgo and Windows/Linux retain existing name/path behavior without those aliases. Windows/Linux use explicit partial process fallbacks and are not live verified
globals.surface: JavaScript Runtime only in this phase; no HTTP or MCP method was added

globals.name: automation
globals.scope: automation.app controls only the current explicit -app execution; the existing App global continues to control external desktop applications.
globals.lifecycle: Native events carry plain data through a bounded queue into the current EventLoop. AppShell contributes AsyncCounts/ResourceCounts/CancelAsync/Wait and releases native UI before the single-instance lease.
globals.singleInstance: Identity is SHA-256 of the required normalized reverse-DNS manifest id. A secondary sends activation and exits after primary ACK without creating a business Execution.
globals.platformBehavior: macOS uses NSStatusItem/NSMenu and per-user flock plus authenticated Unix socket; Windows uses a dedicated Notification Area message loop and per-user ACL named mutex/pipe. Windows GUI/live is not implied by cross-build.

globals.name: Notifications
globals.source: execution-owned Runtime wrapper + macOS UserNotifications own-app model
globals.scope: macOS lists and removes only notifications delivered by the OpenDesk app identity; arbitrary application notifications are not exposed
globals.privacy: title and message are redacted by default and require includeContent=true; metadata stays scoped to OpenDesk
globals.identity: opaque UserNotifications request identifier plus OpenDesk app identity and delivery timestamp; duplicate content is not treated as identity
globals.lifecycle: waitFor uses a bounded own-app poll, prefers new notifications by default, runs under the execution context, and is canceled and joined during teardown
globals.unsupported: activate is not exposed because public UserNotifications APIs report user actions but cannot simulate them; Events does not claim notification.changed
globals.platformBehavior: Windows UserNotificationListener requires manifest capability, package/app identity, and user consent not present in the current OpenDesk host; Linux has no equivalent stable unified backend. Both fail closed.
globals.surface: JavaScript Runtime only; outbound sending remains the existing notify() global

globals.name: window
globals.source: native Window/App owners + polyfills/003-window.js normalization, strict target queries and wait composition
globals.identity: Every observed row has an id. A uniquely resolved row uses platform:pid:native:nativeHandle; metadata-poor or cross-Space rows use platform:pid:unresolved and must not be treated as stable. Title actions resolve a unique current title first and reject duplicate titles.
globals.coordinateSpace: macOS uses global display points with a primary-display top-left origin and possible negative secondary coordinates; Windows uses virtual-screen logical coordinates subject to DPI awareness.
globals.staleTarget: A title action that resolves successfully but loses or renames its target before the backend action reports STALE_TARGET. Initial absence reports NOT_FOUND.
globals.platformBehavior: Existing macOS core paths have historical live fixture evidence, but that does not verify the new target queries/wait. Windows source or packaging evidence is not native Runtime verification; Linux is explicit Unsupported. All calls depend on current capability, permissions and enumerable scope.
globals.surface: The existing JavaScript window facade was extended; no second backend, HTTP route, MCP tool, Accessibility tree, or Spaces manager was added.

targetQueries.target: Explicit object with at most one app/id/pid/exePath/exeName identity and optional exact title, or title alone. No guessed bare string. app delegates to existing App.get and uses all group PIDs; exePath is not App.path and exeName is not App.name.
targetQueries.list: list(target?) is synchronous and returns 0..N observations. Omitted target preserves unfiltered list. Do not discard invalid rows to manufacture uniqueness.
targetQueries.get: get(target) returns Promise<WindowInfo>. Zero matches NOT_FOUND without cause; multiple matches AMBIGUOUS_TARGET; unresolved identity STALE_TARGET; invalid bounds VERIFICATION_FAILED. Wrapped backend errors retain cause, including backend NOT_FOUND. No implicit launch, focus, first-match or title relaxation.
targetQueries.wait: wait(target,{timeout=10000,polling=200,signal?}) snapshots selectors, retries only successful zero-match enumeration, and rejects terminal errors immediately. timeout is integer 0..300000; 0 means one immediate observation. polling is integer 1..10000. Pre-abort does not enumerate. Check deadlines before and after observations; synchronous native calls cannot be forcibly interrupted.
targetQueries.current: Experimental current(WindowInfo) snapshots a resolved id/PID/native handle and directly refreshes only that identity. It never performs title/all-window selection or focus. macOS uses CoreGraphics rather than the high-latency JXA enumeration; a replaced/closed handle is STALE_TARGET.
targetQueries.activate: Experimental activate(WindowInfo,{timeout=1000}) returns immediately when that exact window is already foreground; otherwise it submits at most one PID/title/bounds-qualified native activation and accepts only exact id/PID/native-handle foreground read-back. timeout is 1..10000; no signal, title fallback, replacement window, or repeated activation.
targetQueries.cleanup: Try all owned timer/listener cleanup on every terminal path and settle exactly once even if cleanup fails. cleanupError reports the failure; preserve primary code/cause or reject BACKEND_FAILED instead of false success. No timer creation after registration-time abort.
targetQueries.scopeBoundary: WindowInfo is a current observation, not permanent authority. Querying an id never means it is foreground or safe to click. Compatibility mutations retain title/PID signatures; only current/activate consume an already-resolved full WindowInfo.

globals.name: Screen
globals.notes: Display inventory, pixel, and screenshot methods remain stable. Existing Screen owns display inventory; no duplicate Display global was added. macOS CoreGraphics mode read/list are available and setDisplayMode is Experimental with synchronous readback and caller restore. Brightness is explicitly Unsupported and delegated to hardware-specific Native Extensions. selectRegion/startRecording are Experimental on macOS; audio and frame streaming are explicitly unavailable.

globals.name: System
globals.source: native + execution environment adapter + platform session backend
globals.status: stable reads with experimental session actions
globals.productIdentity: product is a frozen Runtime-owned public identity object with readonly id, name, and website. website is derived from the generated embedded product.odcfg whose sole plaintext maintenance source is configs/product.json; it is not sourced from Execution.env, App Manifest, or a second Runtime URL literal.
globals.sessionSafety: lock, logout, and startScreenSaver require confirm=true before backend access; success returns initiated=true and verified=false because request acceptance is not a postcondition
globals.environmentAccess: getEnv(name, optionalFallback) and hasEnv(name) read only the same per-execution snapshot exposed by Execution.env. They never refresh os.Environ or bypass the empty remote/scheduled environment, and no getAllEnv method is exposed.
globals.sessionIdentity: getSessionState returns only normalized user/session identity and state; unavailable booleans including locked are null rather than inferred
globals.platformBehavior: macOS public CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary supports read-only WindowServer session state and leaves locked unknown; ScreenSaverEngine launch is Experimental while lock/logout are unsupported. Windows uses public LockWorkStation/ExitWindowsEx candidates but remains target-runtime unverified. Linux requires loginctl plus XDG_SESSION_ID and remains target-runtime unverified.
globals.compatibility: existing shutdown, restart, and sleep remain the separate legacy power-control surface; this task does not create a second System or Power namespace

globals.name: Execution
globals.lifecycle: Read-only per-execution context contract; it does not create, cancel, pause, resume, or enumerate executions.
globals.environment: env is a frozen string snapshot. Trusted local -script and ai run executions merge .env, .opendesk.env (or one explicit env file), then the OS environment supplied when OpenDesk started; no login shell or startup file is parsed. Windows names are canonical uppercase. HTTP, MCP, and Scheduler executions receive an empty snapshot by default.
globals.sourcePath: scriptPath is a normalized absolute trusted file path and scriptDir is its parent. Direct -script, ai run, and Scheduler file executions provide them; inline, stdin, HTTP, MCP, and Scheduler inline executions expose null. They are never parsed from source labels.
globals.privacy: env may contain credentials and source/workdir/scriptPath may contain local paths; do not serialize them into logs or remote requests. scriptHash is a correlation aid, not a signature or trust decision.

globals.name: Command
globals.source: native execution owner + platform process-group adapter
globals.availability: Enabled by default for local -script and ai run executions. Disabled for HTTP, MCP, and Scheduler executions.
globals.signature: Command.run(command, args?, {cwd?, env?, envMode?, input?, timeout?, maxOutputBytes?, hideWindow?, signal?}) -> Promise<{exitCode,stdout,stderr}>
globals.capabilities: getCapabilities returns only schemaVersion=1, enabled, supported, and executionScoped=true.
globals.errors: CommandError exposes name, code, exitCode, stdout, and stderr.
globals.safety: run executes an executable directly with an optional argument array. Combined stdout/stderr is bounded; shell interpretation, streaming handles, detached/unref, IPC, and PTY are not exposed.
globals.lifecycle: The enclosing execution stays alive while a command runs. AbortSignal, timeout, and teardown terminate the same execution-owned process group and remove the signal listener.

globals.name: LLM
globals.signature: LLM.generate({prompt|messages, system?, profile?, output?, generation?, timeoutMs?, signal?}) -> Promise<{data,meta}>
globals.profiles: Explicit profile, OPENDESK_LLM_DEFAULT_PROFILE, config defaultProfile, then builtin default. Profiles reference credentials by environment name and never contain the key itself.
globals.capabilities: Side-effect-free and distinguishes supported, configured, executableFound=null, checked=false, authenticated, and available=null. available=null means live availability was intentionally not probed; it is not false.
globals.lifecycle: One total deadline is propagated as an AbortSignal to http.request. Limited transport/status retries remain inside that deadline; protocol and output failures are not retried.

globals.name: Agent
globals.signature: Agent.run({backend?, profile?, prompt, model?, output?, cwd?, timeoutMs?, signal?, backendOptions?}) -> Promise<{data,meta}>
globals.selection: Explicit profile binds backend; explicit backend uses its builtin analysis profile; otherwise environment/config defaults apply and final fallback is codex. Absolute profile/environment executable overrides win. Without one, only builtin codex/claude fixed names are resolved from Execution.env PATH; custom profiles never pass arbitrary names to discovery. Conflict, relative/empty override, missing, non-executable, and unsupported selections fail before process start without fallback.
globals.capabilities: Side-effect-free and distinguishes supported, configured, executableFound, checked=false, authenticated, and available=null. Executable discovery performs only native filesystem metadata/permission checks against the Execution environment; it never launches a version, auth, login, install, or model probe. available=null means live availability was intentionally not probed; it is not false.
globals.lifecycle: Codex JSONL and Claude Code JSON envelopes are independently parsed. Command owns stdin, bounded stdio, timeout, AbortSignal, execution cancellation, and process-tree cleanup. Agent performs no outer task retry.

globals.name: path
globals.source: native path-string helper backed by the execution File WorkDir
globals.compatibility: Common string behavior tracks Node.js 24.15.0 node:path on the target platform. OpenDesk intentionally uses Execution.workdir instead of process.cwd for resolve and relative.
globals.safety: String-only and synchronous: no disk access, existence checks, symlink resolution, tilde/environment expansion, process cwd mutation, or lifecycle resources.

globals.name: File
globals.workdir: File.cwd and every relative File path use the normalized Execution.workdir for this execution.
globals.open: File.open returns a constrained synchronous FileHandle (close, read/readBytes, write/writeBytes, seek, truncate, sync), never a raw host file descriptor. Runtime teardown closes unclosed handles.
globals.json: readJSON and writeJSON are Promise-based; JSON uses Runtime JSON.parse/stringify semantics, has an 8 MiB maximum per operation and 128 container nesting limit.
globals.writeSafety: writeNew exclusively creates a new regular text file through an opened parent directory, rejects an existing final target and symbolic-link/reparse-point parent aliases, rechecks parent identity, and never truncates an existing file. writeJSON remains the existing-file JSON replacement API and has platform-specific atomic-replace support.
globals.realPath: File.realPath resolves an existing path through symlinks/reparse points and returns the canonical absolute host path. It performs no mutation and is used by task persistence to detect redirected internal directories.

globals.name: SQLite
globals.availability: Injected only for trusted local -script, -script-text, -script-stdin, and ai run executions. HTTP, MCP, and Scheduler do not inject SQLite and no generic SQL route/tool is added.
globals.pathResolution: Relative paths use immutable Execution.workdir exactly like File.path. rw is the default and opens an existing file only; rwc permits file creation but never creates parent directories; ro is enforced at SQLite connection level. POSIX backslashes stay literal filename characters; Windows paths use Windows separator/drive/UNC rules. :memory: is isolated per handle and rejects ro. Protected Scheduler database paths (default and direct CLI -scheduler-db) reject PROTECTED_PATH, including resolvable symlink aliases.
globals.values: Parameters use real SQLite binding: sequential ? arrays or exact named parameter objects (names start with a Unicode letter and may then contain letters/digits/_), with null/boolean/string/finite number/SQLite-range BigInt/Uint8Array. BLOB input snapshots before enqueue; unsafe INTEGER output is exact decimal text and BLOB output is Uint8Array.
globals.queryLimits: query defaults to 10000 rows and 8 MiB, configurable up to 100000 rows and 64 MiB; it rejects RESULT_LIMIT instead of truncating. query is not a read-only guarantee: DML RETURNING may write, and a limit/cancel/read error there can report writeState unknown/committed null.
globals.transaction: batch({sql, params?}[]) runs at most 256 single top-level statements in one physical-connection transaction; all success commits, and failure/cancel before commit rolls back. A commit-race error reports writeState unknown/committed null and must not be automatically retried. Raw transaction and connection-changing SQL are rejected.
globals.lifecycle: Each handle has a bounded serialized queue, operation context/timeout/AbortSignal, and an execution-owned worker. close fences new work and waits prior accepted work; execution teardown cancels and releases forgotten handles. SQLiteError carries code, operation, committed, and writeState including unknown outcomes that must not be automatically retried.

globals.name: clipboard
globals.capability: Stable text compatibility API on all supported desktops; experimental rich text, PNG, and file representations currently use NSPasteboard on macOS. clipboard.write verifies every requested representation, clipboard.read returns a changeCount-consistent snapshot, and formats:[] reads metadata only. Binary values are canonical base64, files are absolute paths, and Events clipboard.changed reports metadata only.

globals.name: Webhook
globals.availability: Only trusted local script, App Mode package entry, and local AI executions whose host sets EnableWebhook inject this loopback-only P0 API. HTTP, MCP, Scheduler, and generic Runtime executions fail closed; JavaScript options, Execution.env, and delivery bodies cannot enable it.
globals.summary: Authenticated local short-processing Webhook: current Execution handler, bounded single-flight queue, response waits for handler Promise, and listener-instance delivery dedupe only.
globals.userFlow: Run only OpenDesk JavaScript, copy the generated loopback URL and authorization headers into a real same-machine external HTTP caller, observe its HTTP JSON response plus the OpenDesk delivery log, and press Ctrl+C to revoke the listener. No Go or Node.js installation is required.
globals.appMode: An existing App Mode package entry may call the same Webhook.listen API, but -app apps/opendesk launches the official product package and is not a generic webhook-script entrypoint.

globals.name: NativeExtensions
globals.source: strict manifest registry plus host-generated immutable binding
globals.condition: available to local CLI JavaScript by default after a complete source-free bundle is installed beside the actual executable; the -script path does not affect discovery; HTTP, MCP, and other remote execution transports never inject, enable, redirect, or call it
globals.summary: Discovers strict extension.json bundles from exactly one portable/app-bundled program-relative root; it does not compile or install source examples, generates frozen namespaces and method closures, and starts one validated executable only when a generated method is called.
globals.platformStatus: V1 has Darwin/Linux/Windows implementation candidates; macOS-only examples or Runtime Evidence do not mean the whole API is macOS-only. go-basic is target-buildable Go; macos-vision is macOS-only. A target without target-machine Runtime Evidence is Not Evaluated, not Unsupported.
globals.migration: legacy prototype roots are not scanned or auto-moved/copied/merged/deleted
globals.lifecycle: registry frozen per execution; start a new execution after install or upgrade; no hot reload
globals.errorModel: method failure throws NativeExtensionsError; successful calls return the extension result directly
doesNotExecute: third-party JavaScript facade files during discovery

globals.name: notify
globals.signature: notify(message: string): void; notify(options: OpenDeskNotifyOptions): void
globals.timeout: accepted for compatibility but ignored by current platform notification backends
globals.result: undefined on backend submission success; throws on invalid input or backend failure
globals.validation: options fields use their documented primitive types; timeout must be finite; title and message must be valid UTF-8 without NUL
globals.macOSBackend: native UserNotifications with OpenDesk.app identity; plain CLI and Scheduler re-enter the sibling OpenDesk.app notification-only helper and never use ScriptEditor2/osascript; missing app identity, denied alerts, timeout, helper stderr/exit, and request submission failures throw
globals.sound: sound=true requests the platform default sound; actual sound remains subject to macOS and user settings
globals.visibility: success means NotificationCenter accepted the request after authorization checks; Focus/Do Not Disturb, display sharing/mirroring, and other OS policy may still suppress user-visible presentation

globals.name: Dialog
globals.source: host-owned native binding plus thin polyfill aliases
globals.condition: always injected but DIALOG_DISABLED without the ui capability; CLI needs -ui or trusted config, HTTP additionally needs server enablement, per-request ui and loopback source; Scheduler and MCP have no Dialog opt-in
globals.platformBehavior: macOS normal AppKit top-level window through the existing Custom UI native host; unsupported platforms reject DIALOG_UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM
globals.asyncControlFlow: Promise-only: no onConfirm/onCancel options callbacks and no synchronous EventLoop blocking. await pauses only its async flow; then/catch/finally run on the owner EventLoop. An unobserved Dialog Promise is closed during execution teardown rather than retaining the execution indefinitely; all competing terminal paths settle exactly once.
globals.promptResult: prompt resolves a string on confirm and null on user cancellation. Public examples display a non-sensitive result in a following Dialog.alert; secure or otherwise sensitive input must not be echoed to logs, notifications, or another Dialog.
globals.privacy: secure prompt uses a password input; Dialog never writes message, defaultValue, or prompt input to ordinary logs, errors, summaries, events, or HTTP responses

globals.name: Audio
globals.source: native runtime wrapper + macOS CoreAudio HAL controls + audio pattern matcher/backend seam
globals.capture: not implemented; microphone and systemAudio are explicitly false in capability discovery
globals.patternWatch: experimental contract and bounded in-memory matcher; the default product build currently has no platform capture backend, reports unsupported, and rejects watchSound/waitForSound with NOT_SUPPORTED; source is explicit, raw PCM is neither exposed nor persisted, and a future match is a heuristic wake-up signal rather than a business event
globals.soundCompatibility: Sound keeps blocking MP3/WAV compatibility methods and adds execution-scoped controllable playback sessions
globals.platformBehavior: darwin+cgo uses CoreAudio; non-CGO macOS and other platforms report unavailable and reject instead of silent no-op

globals.name: ui
globals.source: native process driver plus EventLoop bridge plus polyfills/000-ui.js toast facade
globals.condition: always present but dormant by default; local CLI or strict project config authorization is required, while HTTP additionally requires server opt-in, per-request capability declaration, and a loopback peer; new initial positioning is the discriminated position union {mode:absolute,bounds} or {mode:anchor,size,horizontal,vertical}; established absolute bounds remains a compatibility spelling, while the retired top-level size plus placement draft is rejected; WindowHandle placement composes left/center/right with top/center/bottom inside the selected display work area, while setRelativeTo uses current positive logical anchor bounds and a native work-area decision; normal HTML windows can opt into fixed-bridge key events and related surfaces can share an execution-local interactionGroup for outside-interaction notification
globals.platformBehavior: macOS uses the AppKit native host; Windows uses the experimental WinForms/Win32 sidecar, with WebView2 required only for the restricted HTML surface and Dialog, not FloatingWindow or toast; Linux reports available=false and UI creation rejects UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM
globals.preferredFeedback: ui.toast(messageOrOptions) is the preferred OpenDesk-owned transient feedback API. It supports level, timeout, progress, position and returns a ToastHandle.
globals.compatibility: ui.notify(messageOrOptions) remains a deprecated compatibility alias for ui.toast; it is not the operating-system notify() API. Toast callers get state.toast while the historical state.notification field remains available.
globals.capabilities: ui.getCapabilities().window.toast mirrors the existing native window.notify backend capability during the compatibility period.

globals.name: FloatingWindow
globals.source: compact native action-toolbar facade over the Custom UI driver
globals.condition: injected only when Custom UI is explicitly authorized; initial positioning is the discriminated position union {mode:absolute,x,y} or {mode:anchor,horizontal,vertical}. The version-4 ToolbarSpec contains ordered Button, Label, Separator, fixed Spacer, Switch, Checkbox, Input, Select, Slider, SegmentedControl and Progress items, with 1-32 content items horizontally or 1-5 vertically and bounded total items. Controls have stable IDs, fixed 40pt geometry, strict kind-specific payloads, owner-loop value state, native/Accessibility readback and revisioned updates. Input show is nonactivating and never autofocuses; only direct user entry into the native field may activate the host and acquire keyboard focus. Checkbox remains independent selection, while SegmentedControl is the first-class mutually exclusive group; loose Radio and a non-semantic ButtonGroup container are omitted. Button accepts an optional bounded badge string, and standalone Progress supports determinate or indeterminate state. Button icons accept a reviewed built-in name or bounded script-contained PNG/JPEG. Structural items never receive callbacks, state, focus or Accessibility exposure. It reuses shared WindowState, move/close lifecycle events and native draggable readback; conflicting positioning, invalid control/value declarations, unknown fields/items, invalid structure/layout constraints and overflow are INVALID_SPEC

globals.name: Global APIs
globals.summary: 无需 import 即可直接调用的计时器、等待、console 日志、剪贴板快捷函数、取消控制、通知、URL、UTF-8 编解码与 Web Streams 接口。

globals.name: crypto
globals.summary: 当前 Execution 内的安全随机字节与 UUID v4，不启动 Node.js、Python 或第二个 JavaScript Runtime。
